learning_outcomes.title: Angles of elevation and depression
learning_outcomes.statement: Use trigonometric ratios to find side lengths and angle measures of right triangles.
learning_outcomes.rule_summary: Angles of elevation and depression are measured from horizontal lines. Use vertical height differences, including eye height when given.

questions.instruction: A water tower is 110 ft from a student and is 32.5 ft high. The student’s eye level is 6 ft. Find the angle of elevation to the nearest tenth of a degree.
questions.stem: A water tower is 110 ft from a student and is 32.5 ft high. The student’s eye level is 6 ft. Find the angle of elevation to the nearest tenth of a degree.

options.misconception: Use the stated radical, ratio or geometric rule; check reciprocal, sign, squared length and units.
Use the stated radical, ratio or geometric rule; check reciprocal, sign, squared length and units.
Use the stated radical, ratio or geometric rule; check reciprocal, sign, squared length and units.

answer.explanation: The vertical difference is 32.5−6=26.5 ft. θ=tan⁻¹(26.5/110)≈13.5°.

questions.stem: Nabuko is 60 m from a cliff with bridges 100 m high. Her line of sight is 5 m above the ground. Find the elevation angle to the nearest tenth of a degree.

options.misconception: Use the stated radical, ratio or geometric rule; check reciprocal, sign, squared length and units.
Use the stated radical, ratio or geometric rule; check reciprocal, sign, squared length and units.
Use the stated radical, ratio or geometric rule; check reciprocal, sign, squared length and units.

answer.explanation: Use the actual eye-to-top difference 100−5=95 m: θ=tan⁻¹(95/60).
